name: Table of contents
summary: A list of links to the headings on a page, with scrollspy that marks the section being read.
description:
Use it beside long content: docs, articles, legal pages. Put it in a .v-article-aside, or anywhere with .v-sticky so it stays in view.

Without JS it is a plain list of same-page links. data-v-toc marks the link to the section being read with aria-current="location" as the page scrolls, or as the scrolling box the headings sit in scrolls. At the end of the scroller the last section is marked, so a short final section can still be reached.

classes.name: v-toc
classes.description: The <nav>. Give it aria-labelledby pointing at its title.

classes.name: v-toc-title
classes.description: The heading above the list, such as "On this page".

states.description: On a link: the section being read, set by data-v-toc. aria-current="true" from the server looks the same; the JS replaces it once it runs.

hooks.name: data-v-toc
hooks.description: Follows the scroll and marks the current section. Set --v-sticky-top on the nav to move the reading line below a sticky header.

events.name: v:toc
events.description: Fires when the current section changes.

keyboard.action: Moves through the links. Enter follows one: the page scrolls to the heading and focus moves there.

a11y: aria-current="location" tells screen readers which section the reader is in, not only the coloured rule.
Headings need ids. Give them scroll-margin so a sticky header does not cover them after a jump (.v-article-body does this).
Keep the labels the same as the headings, so the list and the page read the same.

examples.title: On this page
examples.description: Nested one level. On a real page the current link follows the scroll; here the targets are not on the page, so nothing is marked.
